{{Quote|Greetings, young Jedi. What brings you to our remote sanctuary?''"<br />"''Unfortunately, the war.''"<br />"''There's no war here. Unless you brought it with you.|Tion Medon and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="SWEIIIROTS" />}}
'''Utapau''' {{Pronounced|'ʔuːtəˌpaʊ}} was an arid [[Sinkhole/Legends|sinkhole]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Utapau system/Legends|Utapau system]] of the [[Tarabba sector/Legends|Tarabba sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Utapau was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'ans]] and the [[Utai/Legends|Utai]], more commonly referred to collectively as [[Utapaun]]s. These species lived in the many giant sinkholes that dotted the planet's scrub-covered surface.

==History==
[[File:PauanNEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'an]].]]
Utapau was a peaceful world that attempted to remain neutral in times of [[List of battles/Legends|galactic conflict]]. The sinkhole world was shared by two symbiotic [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] races whose common ancestors settled the planet at some point after [[57,000 BBY/Legends|57,000 BBY]]. The languid, [[Color/Legends|gray]]-skinned Pau'ans composed only thirty percent of the planetary population but served as the [[Spaceport/Legends|port]] masters, [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucrats]], and patricians of the world. The stubby, humble Utai composed the Utapaun labor class, which maintained the windmills of their sinkhole cities and served as handlers for the native [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyl]] and [[Dactillion/Legends|dactillion]] dragonmounts.<ref name="SEWE" />

Originally, the Pau'ans and the Utai colonists lived separate lives; the Pau'ans on the unremarkable surface, the Utai deep underground. In the 10,000-year span before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the planet's climate began to change, causing stronger and stronger [[Hyperwind storm/Legends|hyperwind storms]]. This forced the Pau'ans to move underground, re-establishing relations with the Utai people and adding their own, unique touch to the Utai cities. The sinkhole communities soon became a mix of Pau'an and Utai architecture, such as the form known as [[Ossic architecture/Legends|Ossic]].<ref name="CL" /> These cities were built into the crevasses and rocky ledges that lined the edges of the sinkholes.<ref name="SEWE" />

The mixed population of Utai and Pau'ans were divided into city states, with occasional border skirmishes and small wars occurring between separate sinkhole communities.<ref name="SEWE" /> However, thanks to the efforts of Utapaun nobles such as [[Timon Medon/Legends|Timon Medon]], the various cities were brought together and Utapau was unified.<ref name="CL" /> To fuel the modest energy needs of the sinkhole cities, many large [[Wind turbine/Legends|windmill]] farms were erected on the wind-blasted surface. These farms were responsible for generating over 99% of the energy consumed by the Utapaun communities.<ref name="SEWE" />

[[File:Pau_City_Sinkhole.png|thumb|right|200px|The massive sinkhole settlement of [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]].]]
During the [[Great Galactic War]], Utapau became one of the many [[Battle of Utapau (Great Galactic War)|battlegrounds]] between the Galactic Republic and the resurgent [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TORHP">{{TORweb|url=info|text=About the Game}}</ref>

Around [[50 BBY/Legends|50 BBY]], an offworld water-[[Mining/Legends|mining]] company discovered supposed healing elements in the underground water lakes of Utapau; the export of this water brought Utapau into the [[galactic community]]. For millennia, a rumor additionally persisted that the planet was one of the birthplaces of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="POTJSB">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> This legend added to the sales pitch, but the water was soon discovered to have no extraordinary powers and the business ended. In the time before the Clone Wars, the planet also served as the headquarters of [[Buuper Torsckil Abbey Devices/Legends|Buuper Torsckil Abbey Devices]].<ref name="SEWE" />

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Chancellor Palpatine thinks Grievous is on Utapau...|[[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]]|<ref name="SWEIIIROTS" />}}
{{Main|Battle of Utapau/Legends}}

Utapau never joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Utapau remained neutral, but allegiance was forced upon the current Master of Port Administration, [[Tion Medon/Legends|Tion Medon]], when [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] and the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] took the world as their own, at the command of [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Grievous threatened to destroy [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] should Tion attempt to call for help, though luckily, [[Jaing Skirata|Jaing]] and [[Kom'rk Skirata]] located Grievous on the planet. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] went to Pau City to spring a trap on the Separatists and was greeted by Tion Medon, who secretly gave Kenobi the location of Grievous's [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]], ''[[Unlimited Projection]]''.

[[File:Utai_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|150px|An [[Utai/Legends|Utai]].]]
General Kenobi sent his [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R4-G9/Legends|R4-G9]] away with his [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] back to the fleet of Republic Ships to make the CIS believe he was leaving. He then attacked Grievous while he was unprepared. During Kenobi's battle with Grievous, [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody's]] forces arrived, including a detachment of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] along with his own soldiers of the [[212th Attack Battalion/Legends|212th Attack Battalion]],<ref name="SWBFII">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> as well as local Utapaun warriors and [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]]. Obi-Wan [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|defeated]] Grievous and the droids. Eventually, Order 66 was issued and Cody followed an unsuccessful attempt to kill Kenobi. The [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], following [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] and the [[Declaration of a New Order]], turned on Obi-Wan, nearly killing him and forcing the Jedi Master to flee Utapau.<ref name="SWEIIIROTS" /> The clone troopers then rounded up members of the resistance movement, including Tion Medon, and deported some to [[Byss/Legends|Byss]], where they were used as slaves in "recolonization efforts".<ref name="EAR">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref>

===Galactic Civil War===
The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] later established a secret storehouse on Utapau, holding artifacts such as the remains of Grievous's body and [[Soulless One/Legends|his starfighter]].<ref name="TSOGGLOW" /> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Utapau was predominantly governed by the [[Fey family]], and there was some [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] influence on the remote world. The [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] had the option to corrupt this world by sending [[Silri]] and a detachment of [[Defiler]]s, 2 [[Missile Attack Launcher]]s (MALs), and [[droideka Mark II]]s to kidnap [[Garnak Fey]] and force the Utapau government to meet the Consortium's demands.<ref name="EAWFOC">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>
Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Utapau was one of the first worlds to become part of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a move designed to prevent the likelihood of once again being attacked and occupied by invading forces.<ref name="TNEGTAS" />

===Second Imperial Civil War===
During the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant|remnants of the Galactic Alliance]] led by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]] set up a base on Utapau after their victory against Sith-Imperial forces on the world of [[Dac/Legends|Dac]]. Following the [[Devastation of Da Soocha]], Sith [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Vul Isen]] and [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Azard]] set up a secret laboratory on the planet where Isen started to study the various species of the planet so as to [[Poison/Legends|poison]] them and destroy the Alliance resistance. He also planned to send a assassin to take out Admiral Stazi before releasing the toxin. Fortunately, Isen's plot was stopped by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Wolf Sazen]] and [[Cade Skywalker]] along with their associates [[Jariah Syn]] and [[Deliah Blue]]. Isen's assassin, a guard in the Galactic Alliance who was [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|paid]] off by the Sith, was killed by Syn and Blue, while Azard was mortally wounded by Sazen in a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] duel, and Vul Isen himself was cut in two by Skywalker before he could poison the planet.<ref name="swl49">[[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]]</ref>

==Military==
[[File:P-38_Fighter.png|thumb|right|200px|The [[Porax-38 starfighter]], a fighter design native to Utapau.]]
From before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Utapau was one of the worlds restricted by a [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] arms embargo on remote galactic regions.<ref name="SEWE" /> Because of this, the local defense fleet was based around downscaled warships only, many of which were designed and built on Utapau itself, including a variant of the [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]] [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|Dreadnaught]]. It was capable of offering some protection against marauding [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], but as a battleship, it was outclassed by those put out by rich, industrialized sectors. For example, each vessel was only about one-fifth the size of a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]]<ref name="ROTSICS" /> and they were all destroyed by the invading Separatist forces.<ref name="SEWE" />

On the other hand, Utapau's primary starfighter, the [[Porax-38 starfighter|Porax-38]], was a tough, long-range snubfighter, designed for Utai pilots and capable of extended interstellar patrols of up to twenty days. They saw good use when the scattered [[Utapau Skyforce/Legends|Utapau Skyforce]] mustered to oust the Separatists alongside Republic forces at the Battle of Utapau.<ref name="ROTSICS" />
In addition to mechanical vessels, the Skyforce also made use of native [[Dactillion/Legends|dactillions]]; giant, flying reptiles that could carry a rider into battle.<ref name="ROTSVD" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Utapau (Kessil system)|Utapau]] was the name for one of the planets (along with [[Aquilae (The Star Wars)|Aquilae]]) that became [[Tatooine]] in the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']],<ref name="Rough Draft">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-star-wars-rough-draft|text=''The Star Wars: Rough Draft''|work=[https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller Starkiller — The Jedi Bendu Script Site]|archivedate=20240601042406}}</ref> the name for Tatooine in the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second]]<ref name="2nd Draft">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/adventures-of-the-starkiller-second-draft|text=Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|archivedate=20240818175509}}</ref> and [[The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller|third]] drafts of the script for ''A New Hope'',<ref name="3rd Draft">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-star-wars-from-the-adventures-of-luke-starkiller-third-draft|text=The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller|archivedate=20240818094359}}</ref> and the name for [[Naboo]] in the revised [[Star Wars: Episode I The Beginning|rough draft]] of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref>

Artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]] envisioned a sinkhole planet during pre-production of ''A New Hope'' in [[1976]], and this artwork was approved by [[George Lucas]] during pre-production of ''Revenge of the Sith''. Digimatte artist [[Brett Northcutt]] who designed Utapau said that he succeeded in creating "the wheat-colored savanna that George and the art directors were looking for."

Author [[Daniel Wallace]] has also pointed out that Utapau is reminiscent of the [[City of Bone]] in the [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel Star Wars]] issue [[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]].<ref name="Blog-danwallace|4">{{Blog|danwallace|4|Weird Stuff about ROTS}}</ref>
